newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dow, dollar hit Brussels bourse, but support seen.
newsitem.headline: Dow, dollar hit Brussels bourse, but support seen.

text.p: The declining dollar and a weaker Dow Jones Industrial Average pushed the Brussels bourse into negative territory on Friday in common with other European markets, but traders said there were buy orders in the dips.
"There has been no big news. The dollar is a bit weaker and people are getting nervous and taking profits," one trader said.
"But there are buying orders under the market so it remains well supported," he added.
"All the European markets are weaker today, it is not just Belgium," another trader said. "If we see the Dow end higher tonight we will start higher on Monday."

Traders said there was no special feature in Friday's Belgian market, although dollar sensitive stocks such as oil major PetroFina, cement maker CBR, retailer Delhaize and non-ferrous metals firm Union Miniere all suffered.
PetroFina ended 3.9 percent lower, CBR lost 3.5 percent, Delhaize fell 2.1 percent and UM dropped 1.3 percent.
But they were far from the only losers on what began as a quiet and directionless day and grew into a busy and depressed one.
There were no gainers at all on the Brussels Bel-20 index of blue chip shares.
The index ended 1.95 percent down at 2,431.48. There were 19 losers and one unchanged.
Outside the index, hamburger chain Quick, which rose strongly through the week on a buy recommendation from a broker, lost 5.7 percent as profit-taking set in.
The busiest issue of the day was steelmaker Cockerill Sambre, which lost 3.1 percent on a volume of more than a quarter of a million shares.
